Recommend optimizer and solver settings for a data set

Source: R/settings_assessment.R
terradish_assess_settings.Rd

Profiles a terradish graph and, optionally, runs short probe benchmarks to recommend optimizer, line-search, solver, and approximation settings for a fitted model. Use this function before a large or slow fit to identify the fastest computational configuration for your data.

Usage

terradish_assess_settings(
  formula,
  data,
  conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
  measurement_model = mlpe,
  nu = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  nonnegative = TRUE,
  optimizer_probe = TRUE,
  solver_probe = TRUE,
  coarse_probe = FALSE,
  optimizer_candidates = c("newton_hager_zhang", "bfgs_hager_zhang", "bfgs_armijo"),
  probe_maxit = 2L,
  factorization = c("simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll", "supernodal_ll"),
  solve_backend = c("matrix", "cholmod_cpp", "cholmod_cpp_cached"),
  coarse_factor = 2L,
  coarse_refine_maxit = 1L,
  loglik_tolerance = 0.001,
  max_seconds = 120,
  cores = 1L,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

formula

Model formula passed to terradish.

data

A terradish_graph object returned by conductance_surface.

conductance_model

Conductance-model factory (e.g. loglinear_conductance).

measurement_model

Measurement model used during optimizer probes. Should match the model you plan to use for the final fit.

nu

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom passed to measurement models that require it (generalized_wishart, wishart_covariance). It is a dispersion parameter that you set, rather than the number of markers: linkage and the population history shared by loci can make effective information much smaller than the SNP count. Use the same value you plan to use for the final fit; it does not change the speed comparison. See the effective-information section of wishart_covariance. Ignored by mlpe and leastsquares.

theta

Optional starting conductance parameter values. If NULL, the default all-zero start is used.

nonnegative

Should regression measurement models constrain the IBR slope to be nonnegative during probes?

optimizer_probe

Logical. Run short optimization probes to compare Newton-Raphson vs. BFGS and line-search algorithms?

solver_probe

Logical. Benchmark direct Cholesky solver settings (factorization style and solve backend) via terradish_solver_benchmark?

coarse_probe

Logical. Include a coarse-raster warm-start probe? Only applicable when data retains its raster stack (saveStack = TRUE).

optimizer_candidates

Character vector of optimizer configurations to probe. Supported entries: "newton_hager_zhang", "bfgs_hager_zhang", "bfgs_armijo".

probe_maxit

Maximum optimizer steps per probe. Keep small (default 2); the assessment compares early iteration cost, not convergence.

factorization

Character vector of Cholesky factorization styles to benchmark when solver_probe = TRUE. Options: "simplicial_ldl", "simplicial_ll", "supernodal_ll".

solve_backend

Character vector of solve backends to benchmark when solver_probe = TRUE. Options: "matrix", "cholmod_cpp", "cholmod_cpp_cached".

coarse_factor

Raster aggregation factor for the coarse-raster probe (passed to the factor entry of approximation_control).

coarse_refine_maxit

Maximum full-resolution refinement steps for the coarse-raster probe.

loglik_tolerance

Maximum log-likelihood difference below the best probe that is still considered acceptable when choosing the fastest option.

max_seconds

Soft wall-time budget in seconds. Each probe that starts before the budget is exceeded is allowed to finish; later probes are skipped.

cores

Number of parallel worker processes passed to probes.

verbose

Logical. Print progress as probes run?

Value

An object of class "terradish_setting_assessment" with components:

profile

A list of graph statistics (number of vertices, edges, focal sites, parameters, and, for smooth_loglinear_conductance, spline-expansion counts.

benchmarks

A list of probe results: optimizer (a data frame with one row per optimizer candidate, or NULL if optimizer_probe = FALSE), solver (a data frame of solver probe results, or NULL if solver_probe = FALSE), and coarse (the coarse-raster probe, or NULL).

reasons

The reason recorded for each recommended setting.

call

The matched call.

defaults

The terradish defaults for the profiled model, after resolving optimizer = "auto" on the expanded conductance parameter count.

comparison

A compact comparison between the recommended settings and the terradish defaults, including a one-line summary.

recommended

A named list of recommended settings: optimizer, control, solver, solver_control, approximation, approximation_control.

notes

Character vector of advisory messages.

A print method summarizes the profile and recommendations.

Details

terradish_assess_settings is an advisory tool, not a model-selection procedure. It does not change package defaults and its output does not affect parameter estimation. Use it to choose computational settings; then fit and interpret your model as usual. It is a speed probe. A fast candidate is not evidence of optimizer convergence, identification, correct standard errors, or biological validity.

Short probes work well for comparing early-iteration cost of different optimizers. They are most informative for large graphs (> 100,000 vertices) where a single function evaluation is slow. For small graphs the default Newton-Raphson + Hager-Zhang settings typically converge in seconds, and assessment adds more overhead than it saves.

The returned $recommended list is intentionally a plain named list of arguments (optimizer, control, solver, solver_control, approximation, approximation_control). You can inspect, edit, or pass it directly:


fit <- terradish(formula, data,
                 optimizer = assessment$recommended$optimizer,
                 control   = assessment$recommended$control,
                 solver    = assessment$recommended$solver)

See also

terradish_solver_benchmark, terradish, slim_terradish

Other solver settings: print.terradish_setting_assessment(), slim_terradish(), terradish_solver_benchmark()

Examples

# \donttest{
# Coarsened for the example. Assessment is most useful on the large graphs
# where solver choice actually matters, so use the full resolution there.
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)

assessment <- terradish_assess_settings(
  Fst ~ forestcover + altitude,
  data = surface,
  measurement_model = mlpe,
  probe_maxit = 2
)
assessment
#> terradish setting assessment
#> Graph: 2531 vertices, 9815 edges, 31 focal sites
#> Conductance parameters: 2 
#> 
#> Recommended settings:
#>   optimizer: newton (fastest acceptable probe: newton_hager_zhang)
#>   line search: HagerZhangControl
#>   solver: direct (fastest direct solver probe: simplicial_ldl + cholmod_cpp)
#>   solver_control:
#> $factorization
#> [1] "simplicial_ldl"
#> 
#> $solve_backend
#> [1] "cholmod_cpp"
#> 
#>   approximation: none (exact full-resolution fit)
#> 
#> Defaults comparison: Assessment differs from terradish defaults: solver_control tuned from terradish defaults.
#> 
#> Optimizer probes:
#>               label elapsed loglik gradient_evaluations hessian_evaluations
#>  newton_hager_zhang    0.20   1495                   10                   4
#>    bfgs_hager_zhang    0.13   1494                    8                   1
#>         bfgs_armijo    0.12   1492                    5                   1
#>  line_search_trials status
#>                   6     OK
#>                   5     OK
#>                   2     OK
#> 
#> Fastest direct solver probes:
#>   factorization      solve_backend setup_time solve_time total_time
#>  simplicial_ldl        cholmod_cpp          0  0.0006257          0
#>   simplicial_ll             matrix          0  0.0000000          0
#>   simplicial_ll cholmod_cpp_cached          0  0.0007256          0
#> 

fit <- terradish(
  Fst ~ forestcover + altitude,
  data = surface,
  conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
  measurement_model = mlpe,
  optimizer = assessment$recommended$optimizer,
  control = assessment$recommended$control,
  solver = assessment$recommended$solver,
  solver_control = assessment$recommended$solver_control
)

smooth_assessment <- terradish_assess_settings(
  Fst ~ forestcover + s(altitude, df = 3),
  data = surface,
  conductance_model = smooth_loglinear_conductance,
  measurement_model = mlpe,
  probe_maxit = 1
)
smooth_assessment$comparison$summary
#> [1] "Assessment differs from terradish defaults: optimizer `bfgs` -> `newton`; solver_control tuned from terradish defaults."
# }
